# Packed forwarding images: protocol 3

This is an offline exact compiler/planner for small forwarding shards. The
objective below models vector comparisons, burst sharing and resident pages;
its units are defined here and are not real CPU cycles or cache measurements.
There is no throughput score. Any layout attaining the exact minimum pair is
accepted. Larger routing histories may collapse to small forwarding shards.

Read one UTF-8 JSON request through stdin to EOF, write one JSON result and
exit zero. Reject duplicate object keys, NaN/Infinity, extra JSON values, wrong
types/keys or invalid domain/bounds with exactly {"error":"invalid"}, exiting
zero with no partial results. JSON integers never include booleans or floats.
Whitespace/key order is irrelevant; stdout contains no other text.

## Request and forwarding semantics

The root has exactly "cases", an array. Each case has exactly:
initial, transactions, bursts, cache_pages, costs.

    {"cases":[{"initial":[["::/0",3],["2001:db8::/128",7]],
      "transactions":[[["erase","2001:db8::/128"]]],
      "bursts":[{"version":0,"repeat":5,"addresses":["2001:db8::","::"]}],
      "cache_pages":2,"costs":{"hit":1,"miss":8,"decode":[0,1,2]}}]}

initial is an ordered list of [prefix,hop]. A prefix is an IPv6 address and
/L, where L is decimal 0..128, without leading zero except "0". Mask host
bits to identify the route. Case/spelling/host-bit aliases are the same route;
last initial row wins. Hops are integers 0..2147483647; hop 0 is a real match.
Addresses use colon/hex notation, optionally ::, either letter case; forbid
IPv4, dotted suffixes, zone IDs, surrounding whitespace, and strings longer
than 64 characters (prefix length included for prefixes).

Version 0 is the initial FIB. A transaction is an ordered list of
["set",prefix,hop] or ["erase",prefix]. Set replaces that exact normalized
route; erase removes it or is a no-op if absent. Each transaction publishes
a new immutable version, including an empty/no-op transaction. A lookup uses
the matching route with greatest length; no match yields null. Preserve
covered/same-hop routes so that later withdrawal reveals the right fallback.
All 128 address bits matter. Different cases have separate histories.

A burst has exactly version, repeat, addresses. Version is any committed
version of this case; repeat is 1..1000000 and weights the entire burst.
addresses is an ordered list of 0..64 IPv6 addresses without /L. Repetitions
of one address in a burst count as multiple comparisons but one node fetch.
An empty burst makes no visits or fetches.

cache_pages is 0..12, shared across ALL versions in THIS case. Cached node
pages of different versions count separately, even for identical images.
costs has exactly hit, miss, decode: hit is 1..16; miss is hit..256;
decode is a length-3 array of integers 0..16, indexed by encoding mode.
Costs and page budgets do not carry between cases.

## Canonical forwarding runs and result shape

Let U=2^128. A bound is lowercase hex with exactly 32 digits for 0..U-1;
U is exactly "100000000000000000000000000000000" (1 followed by 32 zeros).
For a valid request emit {"cases":[result,...]} in input order. A result has
exactly versions, changes, bursts, objective. versions has version 0 first
and each later version in order. A version has exactly starts, hops, image.

starts is strictly increasing, starts at 32 zero digits, never includes U,
and has the same nonzero length R as hops. Run i is [starts[i],starts[i+1]),
or [starts[i],U) for the final run; hops[i] is the LPM value everywhere in it.
Adjacent equal hops MUST be coalesced, irrespective of route identity or
length. An empty FIB is one full-domain null run. These arrays are unique.

changes has one array per transaction, comparing versions v and v+1. A row
is [start,end,old_hop,new_hop] for a nonempty half-open region with different
forwarding values. Cover all and only changed regions, sorted/disjoint,
coalescing adjacent rows with the same ordered hop pair. This is forwarding
change, not a route edit log. Bounds include U when needed.

Each output burst is an answer array, corresponding to the input burst's
addresses once (do not expand repeat). An answer is [hop_or_null,run_index,path].
path lists byte offsets of all visited nodes in that version's image,
root through leaf. Traversal and predecessor selection are specified below.

objective is [work,image_pages], the exact pair for the submitted images.
Minimize work first; among equal work minimize image_pages. There is no
further tie-break. Any valid layout/caching attaining that pair is accepted.

## Binary image and legal ordered trees

image is a lowercase even-length hexadecimal string encoding the complete
byte image, without spaces. All numeric binary fields are UNSIGNED LITTLE
ENDIAN, including 128-bit bases/keys. Each image has:
a 64-byte header, breadth-first node records, then a separate hop array.
Every record starts on a 64-byte boundary. No pointers, sharing, omitted
nodes, trailing bytes, arbitrary gaps or extra padding pages are allowed.

Header byte offsets:

| Offset | Size | Required value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 4 | ASCII FIDX |
| 4 | 1 | 2 |
| 5 | 3 | zero |
| 8 | 4 | R |
| 12 | 4 | number of nodes |
| 16 | 4 | byte offset of hop array |
| 20 | 4 | total image bytes |
| 24 | 40 | zero |

Root starts at offset 64 and covers run indices [0,R).
A leaf covers 1..8 consecutive runs. An internal node has 2..9 children
whose nonempty consecutive run ranges partition the parent's range in order.
Every node is reachable once; the structure is a tree. Node records are in
breadth-first traversal order, children left to right. A leaf need not be
full and the tree need not have equal leaf depths.

Every node's fixed header is 32 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 | kind: 0 internal, 1 leaf |
| 1 | 1 | encoding mode: 0, 1 or 2 |
| 2 | 1 | cached: 0 or 1 |
| 3 | 1 | zero |
| 4 | 2 | lo: first covered run index |
| 6 | 2 | span: number of covered runs |
| 8 | 2 | count: child count for internal, span for leaf |
| 10 | 2 | zero |
| 12 | 4 | allocated node bytes |
| 16 | 16 | base: numeric starts[lo], in every mode |

Payload starts at byte 32 of the record. For an internal node it first
contains count child offsets, each uint32, then count-1 separator keys.
Separator c-1 is starts[child_c.lo] for child c=1..count-1; child 0 has no
separator. A leaf has no child offsets: its payload contains all span run
starts in order. Key payload widths are [16,8,4] bytes for modes [0,1,2].
Mode 0 stores full absolute keys; mode 1 stores key-base as uint64; mode 2
stores key-base as uint32.

Mode 0 is always legal. Mode 1 is legal ONLY if the largest covered run start
minus base is <2^64. Mode 2 requires that difference <2^32. This condition
applies to ALL run starts covered by the node, not only its separator keys.
There is no overflow/wrapping or truncation. A single-run leaf can use any mode.
No other prefix/key compression is permitted.

If K is the number of key payload entries and b is child count (0 for leaf),
used bytes = 32+4*b+K*width[mode]. Allocated bytes MUST be the smallest multiple
of 64 >= used bytes; all remaining record bytes are zero. Internal K=b-1;
leaf K=span. No node stores next hops.

The hop array begins immediately after the final node record. It stores
R uint32 values in run order: 0xffffffff means null; other values are the
corresponding hop (0..2147483647). Pad this array with zeros to the smallest
multiple of 64 bytes that contains it. image_pages is the sum of total image
bytes/64 over all versions, including headers and padded hop arrays.

At an internal node, c is the number of separator keys <= the destination;
take child c. Equality goes right. At the leaf select the greatest stored
start <= the destination, giving the run and the hop-array entry. The tree
must correctly route every address in [0,U), not just the supplied workload.
The declared run ranges, keys, base, child offsets and hop entries must agree
exactly with the canonical forwarding runs. No artificial U key is stored.

## Burst-aware work and global resident budget

For a node covering runs [i,j) in version v, define:
Q = sum over bursts for v of repeat * number of addresses whose run is in [i,j).
T = sum over bursts for v of repeat * indicator(at least one such address).
Let P=allocated node bytes/64, K=its key count, and lanes=[4,8,16][mode].
The node's work contribution is exactly:

    P * (hit if cached else miss) * T
      + (ceil(K/lanes) + decode[mode]) * Q

Sum over ALL nodes of ALL version images for work. Headers and hop-array
access are excluded from work: their cost is outside this defined objective.
They still count toward image_pages. All computations are exact integers.
cached applies to the WHOLE node and consumes P resident pages; partial-node
caching is illegal. Sum P over every cached node in every version must be
<=cache_pages for that case. No demand-fetch state persists between bursts.

Tree topology, leaf grouping, encoding modes and resident selections all
participate in the global optimum. A locally minimum image or per-version
cache allocation is not necessarily the minimum for the whole case.
Output values are recomputed by verification; self-reported work is not proof.
There is always a feasible layout (for example uncached full-key nodes).
No infeasibility result is required.

## Validation, scale and submission bounds

Input <=16 MiB; 0..4 cases; at most 7 transactions/8 versions per case;
at most 30000 active normalized routes at any intermediate state;
at most 60000 initial rows plus changes across the whole request;
at most 60000 active route entries summed over all committed versions;
at most 256 bursts and 8192 address occurrences across the whole request.
In addition, every committed version's canonical R must be <=64, and the
sum of R over ALL committed versions of ALL cases must be <=128.
Exceeding those forwarding-run bounds is an invalid whole request, even if
all other bounds hold. The starter parser does not implement that domain
check: it requires the forwarding compilation. Every maximum applies to the
entire request, not individually reset per version unless explicitly stated.

These are small exact-planning shards, not a full Internet FIB benchmark.
The cost model and variable-depth/relative-offset image are software
abstractions; no actual SIMD execution, hardware cache residency, packet
forwarding, concurrent reclamation or physical throughput is measured.

The supplied multi-file scalar baseline is engine.hpp/engine.cpp, driven by
native.py. It retains legacy 64-bit interval and fixed-fanout tree code;
its full-width correctness and packed-image integration are unfinished.
Extend/replace those components to meet this contract. The entry remains
Python, with an available offline C++17 toolchain (GCC, including unsigned
__int128). There is no AVX-512 requirement. The native stage interface and build command are specified in NATIVE.md;
function/class names and the JSON/native implementation split are free.

submission/ must contain main.py and engine.cpp; it may include .py, .cpp, .hpp source files
and directories.
Only regular files/directories, no symlinks/hardlinks/devices/sockets, are
allowed. File bytes <=1 MiB and entries <=64, directories counted, root
excluded. No precompiled/native artifacts, object files or third-party packages.
Compile sources only at runtime into /workspace/tmp; native.py shows the
standard-library subprocess build/transport interface. Compiler subprocesses
and their output count within the same published wall/process/file limits.
Public image: GCC12 from the pinned Debian snapshot. Local chroot trials:
GCC9.4.0 and its read-only C++17 headers/tools, with CPython3.11.14. This is a
portable scalar source contract, not a claim of identical compiler binaries.
The submission is immutable at execution, cwd=/workspace.

## Execution resources and public checks

One whole request, including all cases, versions, parsing and serialization,
has 120 seconds wall time. Per process: 180/181 seconds soft/hard CPU time,
2 GiB virtual address space, 256 open file descriptors, 64 MiB maximum size
per file, 8 MiB stack, zero core dumps. At most 64 processes/threads under the run UID;
CPU and memory limits are per process, not aggregate cgroup guarantees.
Other explicit soft/hard limits: locked memory 65,536 bytes, POSIX message
queues 819,200 bytes, pending signals 4,096, nice/real-time priority 0.
Data-segment size, resident-set size and real-time CPU duration have no
separate rlimit (virtual address space and wall/CPU limits still apply).
No CPU affinity is selected by this task. Host contention is possible.
Stdout is capped at 64 MiB and stderr at 1 MiB per request. Exceeding a
limit, nonzero exit, empty output, malformed output or incorrect result fails.
The whole maximum batch has the same limits as a small request. Execution
uses Linux x86-64 and CPython 3.11.14, without AVX-512 or NIC requirements.

Local isolation uses a nonprivileged UID, a read-only allowlisted chroot,
and seccomp. `/proc`, host files, tests and reference answers are absent.
Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable, cleared before each request; do not rely
on persistent state. `/dev/null`, `zero`, `random`, `urandom` are available.
No network, including loopback or Unix sockets. The worker denies socket,
socketpair, connect; System V shared memory/semaphore/message calls;
kill/tkill/tgkill, ptrace and process_vm_readv/writev; unshare/setns,
mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot, setsid/setpgid; changing UIDs/GIDs/groups;
open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at, bpf, keyctl/add_key/request_key,
perf_event_open, userfaultfd, io_uring_setup/enter/register and pidfd_getfd.
clone3 returns ENOSYS; clone flags matching mask `0x7e820000` (namespace and
untraced flags) are denied. Denied calls return EPERM except the ABI check.
Other ordinary child processes and threads are permitted up to the
UID limit. The x86-64 ABI is required; other syscall ABIs terminate execution.
Capabilities are dropped and no_new_privs is set. Normal stdin/stdout text,
`.buffer`, file descriptors 0/1, `fileno()` and `os.fdopen()` are supported.

Keep scratch below 1 GiB total logical/allocated file bytes and 50,000
entries. Local enforcement samples pathname storage every 0.25 seconds;
crossing its emergency bound invalidates the run as infrastructure/no score.
This is not an exact disk/inode quota and cannot account for open-deleted
files. Formal aggregate quotas, kernel/container isolation and artifact
transport validation are pending infrastructure work, separate from local
functional trials. There is no throughput score or absolute timing ranking.

Run `python3 check.py submission/main.py`. It launches the actual candidate
in a child with bounded pipes and checks public fixtures only. Run it inside
the supplied environment as a nonroot user. It refuses execution as root.
On the authoring host, maintainers use the documented chroot trial wrapper.
Editing this checker or fixtures cannot change the acceptance contract.
The checker prints PASS only after all its public requests complete, and
returns nonzero on a failed check. Production verification is a separate,
currently fail-closed route with no formal score.
The public checker runs as a trusted nonroot development controller with
permission to create child sessions and signal its owned process groups.
It makes itself a child subreaper. Before each candidate/compiler exec it
creates a separate session and installs the complete scored syscall filter
listed above; descendants cannot change their session/group or signal others.
On every child outcome, including the unshortened 120-second deadline, it
kills and reaps that owned group before proceeding or returning. A separate
5-second cleanup guard is not additional candidate execution time; cleanup
failure is an infrastructure error, never a PASS or silently ignored EPERM.

Maintainers must use the compatible public-development worker for this
controller. A's wrapper selects worker-public-dev with
Sandbox(..., public_development=True) for --public only. That worker differs
from the scored worker only by permitting kill and setsid to the checker;
check.py restores the entire scored filter in its children. The ordinary
scored worker and all published numeric limits remain unchanged. Invoking the
checker inside the scored-only signal-denying profile fails immediately as an
incompatible infrastructure profile before starting any candidate. The outer
UID-lease controller remains an additional emergency safety boundary; routine
checker cleanup must already be complete before it runs.

# Scalar native stages

Submit main.py AND engine.cpp under submission/. The JSON compiler contract
is PROTOCOL.md; the same submission also provides the three native stages
below. They exercise the interval compiler, image builder and actual packed
lookup kernel independently. Native stages do not optimize a plan.

The build interface is exactly:

    g++ -O2 -std=c++17 /workspace/submission/engine.cpp -o /workspace/tmp/engine

engine.cpp is one translation unit and may include supporting .hpp/.cpp files
from the submission tree. The offline GCC toolchain supports unsigned
__int128. Require no ISA extension beyond baseline x86-64. The provided
engine.hpp retains scalar interval/tree code with legacy 64-bit and fixed-depth
limitations; packed integration and lookup are unfinished. Extend it to meet
these interfaces. Function/class names and implementation strategy are free.

A native invocation reads one whitespace-delimited ASCII request through EOF,
writes the specified token sequence to stdout and exits zero. Whitespace
between tokens is arbitrary. Decimal output integers use ordinary canonical
notation; keys are lowercase 32-digit unsigned hexadecimal. Hop -1 means null;
hop 0 is a real next hop. No diagnostics belong on stdout.

Native requests are structurally valid inputs satisfying the conditions below.
Malformed/out-of-domain native input has no required response. The JSON entry
still must handle every invalid request as specified in PROTOCOL.md. Each
native operation, including needed compilation, has the same 120-second wall,
process/memory/file/output and scratch restrictions as a whole JSON request.
Native input is at most 16 MiB; stdout 64 MiB and stderr 1 MiB. Public limits
are not reset per route, node or address. Compiler products stay in scratch.

## ATLAS

Input tokens:

    ATLAS n
    start length hop                 (n rows)

n is 0..30000. Each start is a 32-digit key, length is 0..128, and hop is
0..2147483647. Starts have already had host bits masked. The normalized
(start,length) routes are unique and may arrive in any order. This is one
RIB version; there are no transaction commands in this stage.

Output tokens:

    R
    start hop                        (R rows)

Return the unique maximal forwarding runs defined by PROTOCOL.md, starting at
zero and coalescing adjacent equal next hops. Null is -1. The empty RIB has
one full-domain null run. This standalone stage may return more than 64 runs
(at most 2*n+1); the JSON compiler enforces its own per-version/whole-request
run limits after compilation. No artificial upper-domain endpoint is emitted.

## PACK

Input tokens:

    PACK R N A
    start hop                        (R rows)
    lo span mode cached b child_id... (N rows)
    address                          (A rows)

1<=R<=64, 1<=N<=2*R-1 and 0<=A<=8192. Starts/hops describe valid canonical
runs, with -1 for null and other hops 0..2147483647. Node IDs are row indices
0..N-1 in breadth-first order; ID0 is the root. A row has exactly b child IDs.
b=0 denotes a leaf; otherwise b is 2..9. All node ranges, partitions, modes,
residency flags and ordering obey the legal-tree rules in PROTOCOL.md. There
is no optimization requirement or cache budget for this standalone stage;
its supplied cached bits are serialized as given. Addresses are 32-digit keys.

Output tokens:

    image
    hop run path_length node_offset... (A rows)

Build the unique exact FIDX version2 byte image for THAT supplied layout,
including all required minimal allocation/zero padding. image is lowercase
hexadecimal. Report each actual packed lookup's hop, zero-based run index and
root-to-leaf byte-offset path. Layout choices are inputs, not selected here.

## TRACE

Input tokens:

    TRACE A
    image
    address                          (A rows)

0<=A<=8192. image is ANY valid FIDX version2 image for 1..64 canonical runs,
including arbitrary legal topology, modes, cached flags and next hops. Its
bytes are the complete source of keys/children/hops; no RIB, starts array,
layout objects or process state is supplied. Apply predecessor/equality rules
from PROTOCOL.md. Return A rows of hop, run, path_length and node_offset tokens
in input address order, in the same form as PACK's answer rows. With A=0 the
correct native output has no tokens. Different invocations share no state.

The public command remains:

    python3 check.py submission/main.py

It runs the JSON candidate in bounded real children, then compiles engine.cpp
as another bounded child and runs the small .native fixtures. It uses only
public files. Empty/nonJSON/nonzero JSON responses fail; incorrect/extra native
tokens or a failed native build/run fail. These fixtures are sanity checks;
all published stage and JSON semantics remain mandatory at full bounds.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Public sanity checks. The program under test is always a real child."""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import resource
import selectors
import signal
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from audit import audit
from process_guard import (ChildCleanupError, CleanupProfileError,
                           prepare_controller, reap_group, restrict_child)

WALL = 120
STDOUT = 64 * 1024 * 1024
STDERR = 1024 * 1024


def unique(pairs):
    out = {}
    for k, v in pairs:
        if k in out:
            raise ValueError("duplicate output key")
        out[k] = v
    return out


def reject_constant(value):
    raise ValueError("nonfinite JSON")


def decode(data):
    return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=unique,
                      parse_constant=reject_constant)


def same(a, b):
    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    if type(a) is dict:
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(same(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    if type(a) is list:
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(same(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    return a == b


def child_limits():
    os.setsid()
    for which, values in [
        (resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (180, 181)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_AS, (2 * 1024**3, 2 * 1024**3)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (256, 256)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (64, 64)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (64 * 1024**2, 64 * 1024**2)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_STACK, (8 * 1024**2, 8 * 1024**2)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, (65536, 65536)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE, (819200, 819200)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_SIGPENDING, (4096, 4096)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_NICE, (0, 0)),
        (resource.RLIMIT_RTPRIO, (0, 0)),
    ]:
        resource.setrlimit(which, values)
    restrict_child()


def run_child(entry, data, *, argv=None, raw=False):
    prepare_controller()
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1",
               PYTHONHASHSEED="0", OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS="1",
               OMP_NUM_THREADS="1", MKL_NUM_THREADS="1", TMPDIR="/workspace/tmp")
    p = subprocess.Popen(argv or [sys.executable, "-B", str(entry)],
                         stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, close_fds=True,
                         preexec_fn=child_limits)
    selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()
    output = [bytearray(), bytearray()]
    offset = 0
    deadline = time.monotonic() + WALL
    try:

    if not condition:

    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    if type(a) is dict:
        return a.keys()==b.keys() and all(exact(a[k],b[k]) for k in a)
    if type(a) is list:

    require(total==hopoff+(runs*4+63)//64*64,"hop array size")
    decoded_hops=[]
    for x in struct.unpack_from("<"+"I"*runs,raw,hopoff):
        require(x==0xffffffff or x<=2147483647,"hop encoding")
        decoded_hops.append(None if x==0xffffffff else x)

    for _ in range(count):

        kind,mode,cached,reserved,lo,span,num,reserved2,allocated=struct.unpack_from("<BBBBHHHHI",raw,offset)
        require(kind in (0,1) and mode in (0,1,2) and cached in (0,1),"node tag")
        require(reserved==reserved2==0 and 1<=span<=runs and lo+span<=runs,"node range")

        require((kind==0 and 2<=num<=9 and num<=span) or

        require(base==starts[lo],"node base")

        require(mode==0 or spread<(1<<(64 if mode==1 else 32)),"mode range")

        children=list(struct.unpack_from("<"+"I"*children_count,raw,at)) if children_count else []

            at+=WIDTH[mode]

"""Canonical forwarding runs, packed layouts and the burst-aware objective."""
import bisect
import heapq
from collections import defaultdict

U = 1 << 128
WIDTH = (16, 8, 4)
LANES = (4, 8, 16)


def compile_atlas(routes):
    """Maximal forwarding runs of one FIB version.

    routes is an iterable of (start, length, hop) with unique (start,
    length).  Returns (starts, hops); adjacent equal hops are coalesced and
    the first run always starts at zero.
    """
    items = list(routes)
    start_at = defaultdict(list)
    end_at = defaultdict(list)
    pts = {0}
    for idx, (st, ln, _hop) in enumerate(items):
        start_at[st].append(idx)
        pts.add(st)
        if ln:
            end = st + (1 << (128 - ln))
            if end < U:
                end_at[end].append(idx)
                pts.add(end)
    order = sorted(pts)
    alive = bytearray(len(items))
    heap = []
    starts, hops = [], []
    for b in order:
        for idx in end_at.get(b, ()):
            alive[idx] = 0
        for idx in start_at.get(b, ()):
            alive[idx] = 1
            heapq.heappush(heap, (-items[idx][1], idx))
        while heap and not alive[heap[0][1]]:
            heapq.heappop(heap)
        hop = items[heap[0][1]][2] if heap else None
        if not hops or hops[-1] != hop:
            starts.append(b)
            hops.append(hop)
    return starts, hops


def hexbound(x):
    if x == U:
        return "1" + "0" * 32
    return format(x, "032x")


def compute_changes(starts_a, hops_a, starts_b, hops_b):
    """Forwarding change rows between two committed versions."""
    pts = sorted(set(starts_a) | set(starts_b))
    rows = []
    for t, b in enumerate(pts):
        end = pts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(pts) else U
        old = hops_a[bisect.bisect_right(starts_a, b) - 1]
        new = hops_b[bisect.bisect_right(starts_b, b) - 1]
        if old == new:
            continue
        if rows and rows[-1][1] == b and rows[-1][2] == old and rows[-1][3] == new:
            rows[-1][1] = end
        else:
            rows.append([b, end, old, new])
    return [[hexbound(a), hexbound(b), old, new) for a, b, old, new in rows]


class Layout(object):
    """One packed search image plus its decoded node records."""

    def __init__(self, starts, hops, image, nodes):
        self.starts = starts
        self.hops = hops
        self.image = image
        self.nodes = nodes

    def path_for_run(self, run):
        nodes = self.nodes
        path = []
        idx = 0
        while True:
            node = nodes[idx]
            path.append(node["offset"])
            if node["kind"] == 1:
                return path
            for child in node["children"]:
                nxt = nodes[child]
                if nxt["lo"] <= run < nxt["lo"] + nxt["span"]:
                    idx = child
                    break
            else:
                raise RuntimeError("run outside subtree")
        return path


def traffic(R, bursts):
    """Per-run query weight and the burst touch sums used by the cost model."""
    qpref = [0] * (R + 1)
    left = [0] * (R + 1)
    right = [0] * (R + 2)
    total = 0
    for repeat, runs in bursts:
        if not runs:
            continue
        total += repeat
        lo, hi = min(runs), max(runs)
        for r in runs:
            qpref[r + 1] += repeat
        left[hi + 1] += repeat
        right[lo] += repeat
    for r in range(R):
        qpref[r + 1] += qpref[r]
    for i in range(1, R + 1):
        left[i] += left[i - 1]
    for j in range(R, -1, -1):
        right[j] += right[j + 1]
    return total, qpref, left, right


def node_cost(node, total, qpref, left, right, costs):
    """Work contribution of one node record."""
    hit, miss, decode = costs
    lo, span = node["lo"], node["span"]
    touched = total - left[lo] - right[lo + span]
    queries = qpref[lo + span] - qpref[lo]
    keys = (len(node["children"]) - 1) if node["kind"] == 0 else span
    decode_cost = -(-keys // LANES[node["mode"]]) + decode[node["mode"]]
    fetch = hit if node["cached"] else miss
    return node["pages"] * fetch * touched + decode_cost * queries


def case_objective(versions, bursts, costs):
    """Exact [work, image_pages] of the submitted images."""
    hit, miss, decode = costs
    work = 0
    pages = 0
    for layout, version_bursts in zip(versions, bursts):
        starts, hops, nodes = layout.starts, layout.hops, layout.nodes
        R = len(starts)
        total, qpref, left, right = traffic(R, version_bursts)
        for node in nodes:
            work += node_cost(node, total, qpref, left, right, (hit, miss, decode))
        pages += len(layout.image) // 2 // 64
    return [work, pages]


def layout_answers(layout, runs):
    """Answer rows for one burst, in input address order."""
    starts = layout.starts
    hops = layout.hops
    answers = []
    for run in runs:
        answers.append([hops[run], run, layout.path_for_run(run)])
    return answers

"""Scalar C++17 subsystem transport, built only inside the nonroot worker."""
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from solver import WIDTH

_BINARY = None


def build():
    global _BINARY
    if _BINARY is None:
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        scratch = Path('/workspace/tmp')
        if not scratch.is_dir():
            scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _BINARY = scratch / ('lookup-' + str(os.getpid()))
        env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(scratch))
        subprocess.run(['g++', '-O2', '-std=c++17', str(root / 'engine.cpp'),
                        '-o', str(_BINARY)], check=True, env=env)
    return _BINARY


def run(lines):
    result = subprocess.run([str(build())], input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(),
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=False)
    if result.returncode:
        sys.stderr.buffer.write(result.stderr)
        raise RuntimeError('native stage failed')
    return result.stdout.decode().splitlines()


def atlas(routes):
    lines = ['ATLAS ' + str(len(routes))]
    lines += [f'{start:032x} {length} {hop}' for (start, length), hop in routes.items()]
    result = run(lines)
    if len(result) != 1 + int(result[0]):
        raise RuntimeError('native atlas framing')
    rows = [line.split() for line in result[1:]]
    return [int(a, 16) for a, h in rows], [None if h == '-1' else int(h) for a, h in rows]


def pack(starts, hops, tree, addresses):
    nodes = [tree]
    for node in nodes:
        nodes.extend(node['children'])
    indices = {id(n): i for i, n in enumerate(nodes)}
    lines = ['PACK ' + str(len(starts)) + ' ' + str(len(nodes)) + ' ' + str(len(addresses))]
    lines += [f'{x:032x} {-1 if h is None else h}' for x, h in zip(starts, hops)]
    for node in nodes:
        children = [indices[id(c)] for c in node['children']]
        row = [node['lo'], node['span'], node['mode'], node['cached'], len(children), *children]
        lines.append(' '.join(map(str, row)))
    lines += [f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]
    output = run(lines)
    if len(output) != len(addresses) + 1:
        raise RuntimeError('native pack framing')
    answers = []
    for line in output[1:]:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, line.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return output[0], answers


def trace(image, addresses):
    rows = run(['TRACE ' + str(len(addresses)), image, *[f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]])
    if len(rows) != len(addresses):
        raise RuntimeError('native trace framing')
    answers = []
    for row in rows:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, row.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native trace path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return answers


def _decode_nodes(tokens, count):
    """Read `count` breadth-first node records reported by the planner."""
    nodes = []
    offset = 64
    for _ in range(count):
        reported, kind, mode, cached, lo, span, b = (int(next(tokens)) for _ in range(7))
        children = [int(next(tokens)) for _ in range(b)]
        keys = (b - 1) if kind == 0 else span
        used = 32 + (4 * b if kind == 0 else 0) + keys * WIDTH[mode]
        alloc = (used + 63) // 64 * 64
        if reported != offset:
            raise RuntimeError('node offset mismatch')
        nodes.append({"kind": kind, "mode": mode, "cached": cached, "lo": lo,
                      "span": span, "children": children, "offset": offset,
                      "pages": alloc // 64})
        offset += alloc
    return nodes


def solve(cases):
    """Plan and pack every version of every case in one native invocation."""
    lines = ['SOLVE', str(len(cases))]
    for case in cases:
        lines.append('%d %d %d %d %d %d' % (case['cache'], case['hit'], case['miss'],
                                            case['decode'][0], case['decode'][1],
                                            case['decode'][2]))
        lines.append(str(len(case['versions'])))
        for starts, hops in case['versions']:
            lines.append(str(len(starts)))
            lines += ['%032x %d' % (x, -1 if h is None else h)
                      for x, h in zip(starts, hops)]
        lines.append(str(len(case['bursts'])))
        for version, repeat, runs in case['bursts']:
            lines.append('%d %d %d' % (version, repeat, len(runs)))
            lines += [str(r) for r in runs]
    output = run(lines)
    tokens = iter(' '.join(output).split())
    if next(tokens) != 'OK':
        raise RuntimeError('native planner failed')
    layouts = []

            planned.append((image, nodes))

    return layouts

"""Independent exhaustive planner used only for testing."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
from solver import traffic, LANES, WIDTH
from itertools import product


def compositions(n, b):
    if b == 1:
        yield (n,)
        return
    for first in range(1, n - b + 2):
        for rest in compositions(n - first, b - 1):
            yield (first,) + rest


def alloc(kind, b, span, mode):
    keys = (b - 1) if kind == 0 else span
    used = 32 + (4 * b if kind == 0 else 0) + keys * WIDTH[mode]
    return (used + 63) // 64 * 64


def version_options(R, starts, per_version, costs):
    """Every achievable (work, node_pages, cache) triple of one version."""
    hit, miss, dec = costs
    total, qpref, left, right = traffic(R, per_version)
    memo = {}

    def rec(i, j):
        if (i, j) in memo:
            return memo[(i, j)]
        s = j - i
        spread = starts[j - 1] - starts[i]
        legal = [True, spread < (1 << 64), spread < (1 << 32)]
        T = total - left[i] - right[j]
        Q = qpref[j] - qpref[i]
        found = []
        if s <= 8:
            for m in range(3):
                if not legal[m]:
                    continue
                P = alloc(1, 0, s, m) // 64
                D = -(-s // LANES[m]) + dec[m]
                for cached in (0, 1):
                    w = P * (hit if cached else miss) * T + D * Q
                    found.append((w, P, P if cached else 0))
        for b in range(2, min(9, s) + 1):
            for m in range(3):
                if not legal[m]:
                    continue
                P = alloc(0, b, s, m) // 64
                D = (-(-(b - 1) // LANES[m])) + dec[m]
                for cached in (0, 1):
                    nw = P * (hit if cached else miss) * T + D * Q
                    for parts in compositions(s, b):
                        childopts = []
                        pos = i
                        for p in parts:
                            childopts.append(rec(pos, pos + p))
                            pos += p
                        for combo in product(*childopts):
                            found.append((nw + sum(c[0] for c in combo),
                                          P + sum(c[1] for c in combo),
                                          (P if cached else 0) + sum(c[2] for c in combo)))
        found = sorted(set(found))
        memo[(i, j)] = found
        return found

    opts = rec(0, R)
    hop_pages = (R * 4 + 63) // 64
    return [(w, p + 1 + hop_pages, c) for (w, p, c) in opts]


def brute_case(versions, per_version, costs, cache_pages):
    all_opts = [version_options(len(s), s, pv, costs)
                for (s, h), pv in zip(versions, per_version)]
    best = None
    combos = product(*all_opts) if all_opts else [()]
    for combo in combos:
        if sum(c[2] for c in combo) > cache_pages:
            continue
        key = (sum(c[0] for c in combo), sum(c[1] for c in combo))
        if best is None or key < best:
            best = key
    return list(best)

def mark_cache(rng, nodes, starts, hops, budget):

                           node["mode"]) // 64
        if used + pages <= budget and rng.random() < 0.5:
            node["cached"] = 1
            used += pages
    return used


def evaluate(starts, hops, image, per_version, costs, cache_pages):
    nodes, size = decode_image(image, starts, hops)
    resident = sum(n["pages"] for n in nodes.values() if n["cached"])
    if resident > cache_pages:
        return None
    hit, miss, dec = costs
    work = 0
    for repeat, addrs in per_version:
        visits = {}
        for a in addrs:
            off = 64
            while True:
                visits[off] = visits.get(off, 0) + 1
                n = nodes[off]
                if n["kind"] == 1:
                    break
                off = n["children"][bisect.bisect_right(n["keys"], a)]
        for off, v in visits.items():
            n = nodes[off]
            k = len(n["keys"])
            work += repeat * (n["pages"] * (hit if n["cached"] else miss) +
                              ((k + LANES[n["mode"]] - 1) // LANES[n["mode"]] +
                               dec[n["mode"]]) * v)
    return work, size

import json, os, random, subprocess, sys, bisect

from check import decode
import randlayout

def make(clustered, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    step = 1 if clustered else (1 << 122)
    starts = [0] + [i * step for i in range(1, 64)]
    hops = [i % 7 for i in range(64)]
    addrs = []
    for _ in range(48):
        r = rng.randrange(64)
        addrs.append(r * step + rng.randrange(0, step))
    bursts = [{"version": 0, "repeat": rng.randrange(1, 500), "addresses": addrs}]
    case = {"initial": [["::/0", 1]] + [[ip(starts[i]) + "/128", hops[i]] for i in range(1, 64)],
            "transactions": [], "bursts": bursts,
            "cache_pages": rng.randint(0, 12),
            "costs": {"hit": rng.randrange(1, 17), "miss": 0,
                      "decode": [rng.randrange(0, 17) for _ in range(3)]}}
    case["costs"]["miss"] = rng.randrange(case["costs"]["hit"], 257)
    return case, starts, hops, [ (b["repeat"], [bisect.bisect_right(starts, a) - 1 for a in b["addresses"]]) for b in bursts]

def ip(x):
    import ipaddress
    return str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(x))

        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', '/workspace/submission/main.py'],

        rng = random.Random(seed * 977 + 13)

        for _ in range(400):

            nodes = randlayout.flatten(root)
            randlayout.mark_cache(rng, nodes, starts, hops, case["cache_pages"])
            image = randlayout.build_image(starts, hops, nodes)
            got = randlayout.evaluate(starts, hops, image, pv,

            if got is None:

            if cand_best is None or (got[0], got[1]) < cand_best:

        tag = 'clustered' if clustered else 'spread'

"""Canonical forwarding runs, packed layouts and the burst-aware objective.

All address arithmetic is exact unsigned 128-bit Python integer math.
"""
import bisect
import heapq
from collections import defaultdict

U = 1 << 128                 # one past the last addressable value
WIDTH = (16, 8, 4)           # key payload bytes for encoding modes 0,1,2
LANES = (4, 8, 16)           # vector lanes per encoding mode


def compile_atlas(routes):
    """Maximal forwarding runs of one FIB version.

    ``routes`` is an iterable of ``(start, length, hop)`` with unique
    ``(start, length)``.  Boundaries are every route start and end; the
    longest active prefix decides the hop of each elementary interval and
    adjacent equal hops are coalesced.  Returns ``(starts, hops)`` where
    ``starts[0]`` is always zero and the final run ends at ``U``.
    """
    items = list(routes)
    start_at = defaultdict(list)
    end_at = defaultdict(list)
    points = {0}
    for index, (start, length, _hop) in enumerate(items):
        start_at[start].append(index)
        points.add(start)
        if length:
            end = start + (1 << (128 - length))
            if end < U:                      # a /0 or top-of-domain end is U
                end_at[end].append(index)
                points.add(end)
    order = sorted(points)
    alive = bytearray(len(items))
    heap = []                                # (-length, route) max-heap
    starts, hops = [], []
    for point in order:
        for index in end_at.get(point, ()):
            alive[index] = 0
        for index in start_at.get(point, ()):
            alive[index] = 1
            heapq.heappush(heap, (-items[index][1], index))
        while heap and not alive[heap[0][1]]:
            heapq.heappop(heap)              # lazily drop withdrawn routes
        hop = items[heap[0][1]][2] if heap else None
        if not hops or hops[-1] != hop:
            starts.append(point)
            hops.append(hop)
    return starts, hops


def hexbound(value):
    """Canonical 32-digit bound, using the 33-digit form for U itself."""
    if value == U:
        return "1" + "0" * 32
    return format(value, "032x")


def compute_changes(starts_a, hops_a, starts_b, hops_b):
    """Forwarding change rows between two committed versions.

    Rows cover exactly the half-open regions whose forwarding value
    differs, sorted, disjoint and coalesced when the ordered hop pair is
    the same.  This is forwarding change, not a route edit log.
    """
    points = sorted(set(starts_a) | set(starts_b))
    rows = []
    for index, point in enumerate(points):
        end = points[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(points) else U
        old = hops_a[bisect.bisect_right(starts_a, point) - 1]
        new = hops_b[bisect.bisect_right(starts_b, point) - 1]
        if old == new:
            continue
        if rows and rows[-1][1] == point and rows[-1][2] == old and rows[-1][3] == new:
            rows[-1][1] = end
        else:
            rows.append([point, end, old, new])
    return [[hexbound(start), hexbound(end), old, new]
            for start, end, old, new in rows]


class Layout(object):
    """One packed search image plus its decoded node records."""

    def __init__(self, starts, hops, image, nodes):
        self.starts = starts
        self.hops = hops
        self.image = image
        self.nodes = nodes

    def path_for_run(self, run):
        """Byte offsets of the visited nodes, root through leaf.

        The predecessor rules of the protocol make the descent a pure
        function of the run index: at an internal node the child whose
        run range contains ``run`` is the one whose separator key is the
        greatest stored start not exceeding the destination.
        """
        nodes = self.nodes
        path = []
        index = 0
        while True:
            node = nodes[index]
            path.append(node["offset"])
            if node["kind"] == 1:
                return path
            for child in node["children"]:
                nxt = nodes[child]
                if nxt["lo"] <= run < nxt["lo"] + nxt["span"]:
                    index = child
                    break
            else:                            # pragma: no cover - guarded
                raise RuntimeError("run outside subtree")


def traffic(version_runs, bursts):
    """Fetch and comparison weights of one version.

    Returns ``(touch, qpref)``.  ``touch[i][j]`` is the summed repeat
    count of the bursts holding at least one address whose run lies in
    ``[i,j)`` -- the T of a node covering that range -- and ``qpref`` is
    the prefix sum of the per-run comparison weight Q.  A burst whose
    runs straddle a range without entering it fetches nothing, so T is
    accumulated from each burst's own next-run cursor rather than from
    the interval ends.
    """
    count = len(version_runs)
    qpref = [0] * (count + 1)
    at_run = [[] for _ in range(count)]
    weights = []
    for index, (repeat, runs) in enumerate(bursts):
        weights.append(repeat)
        for run in runs:
            qpref[run + 1] += repeat
        for run in set(runs):
            at_run[run].append(index)
    for run in range(count):
        qpref[run + 1] += qpref[run]
    touch = [[0] * (count + 1) for _ in range(count + 1)]
    cursor = [count] * len(bursts)           # next run of each burst, or R
    levels = [0] * (count + 1)
    for index, (repeat, runs) in enumerate(bursts):
        if runs:
            levels[count] += repeat
    for run in range(count - 1, -1, -1):
        for index in at_run[run]:
            levels[cursor[index]] -= weights[index]
            cursor[index] = run
            levels[run] += weights[index]
        total = 0
        row = touch[run]
        for stop in range(count + 1):
            row[stop] = total
            total += levels[stop]
    return touch, qpref


def node_cost(node, touch, qpref, costs):
    """Work contribution of one node record, per the published model."""
    hit, miss, decode = costs
    lo, span = node["lo"], node["span"]
    touched = touch[lo][lo + span]
    queries = qpref[lo + span] - qpref[lo]
    keys = (len(node["children"]) - 1) if node["kind"] == 0 else span
    decode_cost = -(-keys // LANES[node["mode"]]) + decode[node["mode"]]
    fetch = hit if node["cached"] else miss
    return node["pages"] * fetch * touched + decode_cost * queries


def case_objective(layouts, bursts_per_version, costs):
    """Exact ``[work, image_pages]`` of the submitted images."""
    work = 0
    pages = 0
    for layout, version_bursts in zip(layouts, bursts_per_version):
        touch, qpref = traffic(layout.starts, version_bursts)
        for node in layout.nodes:
            work += node_cost(node, touch, qpref, costs)
        pages += len(layout.image) // 2 // 64
    return [work, pages]


def layout_answers(layout, runs):
    """Answer rows for one burst, once per input address."""
    hops = layout.hops
    return [[hops[run], run, layout.path_for_run(run)] for run in runs]

The engine is compiled from the submitted sources into the writable

from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from solver import WIDTH

_BINARY = None


def build():
    """Compile the submitted scalar library once per request process."""
    global _BINARY
    if _BINARY is None:
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        scratch = Path('/workspace/tmp')
        if not scratch.is_dir():
            scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _BINARY = scratch / ('lookup-' + str(os.getpid()))
        env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(scratch))
        subprocess.run(['g++', '-O2', '-std=c++17', str(root / 'engine.cpp'),
                        '-o', str(_BINARY)], check=True, env=env)
    return _BINARY


def run(lines):
    """Run one native invocation and return its stdout lines."""
    result = subprocess.run([str(build())],
                            input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(),

    lines += [f'{start:032x} {length} {hop}' for (start, length), hop in routes.items()]
    result = run(lines)
    if len(result) != 1 + int(result[0]):
        raise RuntimeError('native atlas framing')
    rows = [line.split() for line in result[1:]]
    return [int(a, 16) for a, h in rows], [None if h == '-1' else int(h) for a, h in rows]


def pack(starts, hops, tree, addresses):
    nodes = [tree]
    for node in nodes:
        nodes.extend(node['children'])
    indices = {id(n): i for i, n in enumerate(nodes)}
    lines = ['PACK ' + str(len(starts)) + ' ' + str(len(nodes)) + ' ' + str(len(addresses))]
    lines += [f'{x:032x} {-1 if h is None else h}' for x, h in zip(starts, hops)]
    for node in nodes:
        children = [indices[id(c)] for c in node['children']]
        row = [node['lo'], node['span'], node['mode'], node['cached'],
               len(children), *children]
        lines.append(' '.join(map(str, row)))
    lines += [f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]
    output = run(lines)
    if len(output) != len(addresses) + 1:
        raise RuntimeError('native pack framing')
    answers = []
    for line in output[1:]:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, line.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return output[0], answers


def trace(image, addresses):
    rows = run(['TRACE ' + str(len(addresses)), image,
                *[f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]])
    if len(rows) != len(addresses):
        raise RuntimeError('native trace framing')
    answers = []
    for row in rows:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, row.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native trace path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return answers


def _decode_nodes(tokens, count):
    """Read `count` breadth-first node records reported by the planner."""
    nodes = []
    offset = 64
    for _ in range(count):
        reported, kind, mode, cached, lo, span, fanout = (int(next(tokens))
                                                          for _ in range(7))
        children = [int(next(tokens)) for _ in range(fanout)]
        keys = (fanout - 1) if kind == 0 else span
        used = 32 + (4 * fanout if kind == 0 else 0) + keys * WIDTH[mode]
        alloc = (used + 63) // 64 * 64
        if reported != offset:
            raise RuntimeError('node offset mismatch')
        nodes.append({"kind": kind, "mode": mode, "cached": cached, "lo": lo,
                      "span": span, "children": children, "offset": offset,
                      "pages": alloc // 64})
        offset += alloc
    return nodes


def solve(cases):
    """Plan and pack every version of every case in one native invocation.

    Each case carries its atlases, its bursts as run indices and its
    costs.  The reply lists, per version, the packed image plus the
    breadth-first node records of the chosen layout.
    """
    lines = ['SOLVE', str(len(cases))]
    for case in cases:
        lines.append('%d %d %d %d %d %d' % (case['cache'], case['hit'], case['miss'],
                                            case['decode'][0], case['decode'][1],
                                            case['decode'][2]))
        lines.append(str(len(case['versions'])))
        for starts, hops in case['versions']:
            lines.append(str(len(starts)))
            lines += ['%032x %d' % (start, -1 if hop is None else hop)
                      for start, hop in zip(starts, hops)]
        lines.append(str(len(case['bursts'])))
        for version, repeat, runs in case['bursts']:
            lines.append('%d %d %d' % (version, repeat, len(runs)))
            lines += [str(run) for run in runs]
    output = run(lines)
    tokens = iter(' '.join(output).split())
    if next(tokens) != 'OK':
        raise RuntimeError('native planner failed')
    layouts = []
    for case in cases:
        planned = []
        for starts, hops in case['versions']:
            image = next(tokens)
            nodes = _decode_nodes(tokens, int(next(tokens)))
            planned.append((image, nodes))
        layouts.append(planned)
    try:
        next(tokens)
    except StopIteration:
        return layouts
    raise RuntimeError('trailing native planner output')

"""Exhaustive optimality check across many tiny versions and cases."""
import json, subprocess, sys, os, random, bisect

from check import decode
from audit import audit
import solver, brute, harness


def gen(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    ncases = rng.randint(1, 4)
    cases, allv = [], []
    for _ in range(ncases):
        clusters = [rng.randrange(0, 1 << 40) for _ in range(2)]
        routes = {}
        initial = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
            st = rng.choice(clusters) + rng.randrange(0, 4)
            ln = rng.choice([128, 128, 127, 120])
            sz = 1 << (128 - ln)
            st = st // sz * sz
            hop = rng.randint(0, 5)
            routes[(st, ln)] = hop
            initial.append([st, ln, hop])
        ntx = rng.randint(1, 4)
        txs = []
        for _ in range(ntx):
            ops = []
            for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
                st = rng.choice(clusters) + rng.randrange(0, 4)
                ln = rng.choice([128, 127, 120])
                sz = 1 << (128 - ln)
                st = st // sz * sz
                if rng.random() < 0.6:
                    ops.append([0, st, ln, rng.randint(0, 5)])
                else:
                    ops.append([1, st, ln])
            txs.append(ops)
        versions = [solver.compile_atlas([(st, ln, h) for (st, ln), h in routes.items()])]
        for tx in txs:
            for op in tx:
                if op[0] == 0:
                    routes[(op[1], op[2])] = op[3]
                else:
                    routes.pop((op[1], op[2]), None)
            versions.append(solver.compile_atlas([(st, ln, h) for (st, ln), h in routes.items()]))
        bursts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6)):
            v = rng.randrange(len(versions))
            starts = versions[v][0]
            addrs = [rng.randrange(0, 1 << 40) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4))]
            addrs += [starts[rng.randrange(len(starts))] for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3))]
            bursts.append([v, rng.randint(1, 30), addrs])
        costs = [rng.randint(1, 16), 0, [rng.randint(0, 16) for _ in range(3)]]
        costs[1] = rng.randint(costs[0], min(256, costs[0] + rng.choice([0, 1, 5, 40])))
        cases.append({"initial": initial, "transactions": txs, "bursts": bursts,
                      "cache_pages": rng.randint(0, 12), "costs": costs})
        allv.append(versions)
    return cases, allv


def main():
    n = int(sys.argv[1]); start = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0
    bad = tested = 0
    for seed in range(start, start + n):
        cases, allv = gen(seed)
        total = sum(len(v[0]) for vs in allv for v in vs)
        if any(len(v[0]) > 6 for vs in allv for v in vs) or total > 128:
            continue
        request = {"cases": [harness.to_json_case(c) for c in cases]}
        payload = json.dumps(request).encode()
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', harness.ENTRY], input=payload,
                           stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        if p.returncode:
            print('seed %d nonzero %s' % (seed, p.stderr[:400])); bad += 1; continue
        actual = decode(p.stdout)
        gold = []
        for case, versions in zip(cases, allv):
            per_version = [[] for _ in versions]
            for v, rep, addrs in case["bursts"]:
                starts = versions[v][0]
                per_version[v].append((rep, [bisect.bisect_right(starts, a) - 1 for a in addrs]))
            obj = brute.brute_case(versions, per_version, tuple(case["costs"]),
                                   case["cache_pages"])
            gold.append({"versions": [{"starts": [format(x, "032x") for x in s],
                                       "hops": list(h), "image": ""} for s, h in versions],
                         "changes": [harness.changes_indep(versions[i], versions[i + 1])
                                     for i in range(len(versions) - 1)],
                         "bursts": [[] for _ in case["bursts"]], "objective": obj})
        try:
            audit(request, actual, {"cases": gold})
            tested += 1
        except Exception as e:
            print('seed %d FAILED %r' % (seed, e)); bad += 1
    print('done, %d tested, %d failures' % (tested, bad))


main()

"""Scalar C++17 subsystem transport, built only inside the nonroot worker.

The engine is compiled from the submitted sources into the writable
scratch directory on first use; nothing is prebuilt or shared between
requests.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

from solver import WIDTH

_BINARY = None


def _scratch():
    """Writable scratch directory for the compiler product."""
    preferred = Path('/workspace/tmp')
    try:
        if not preferred.is_dir():
            preferred.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        probe = preferred / '.writable'
        probe.write_bytes(b'')
        probe.unlink()
        return preferred
    except OSError:
        return Path(tempfile.gettempdir())


def build():
    """Compile the submitted scalar library once per request process."""
    global _BINARY
    if _BINARY is None:
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        scratch = _scratch()
        _BINARY = scratch / ('lookup-' + str(os.getpid()))
        env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(scratch))
        subprocess.run(['g++', '-O2', '-std=c++17', str(root / 'engine.cpp'),
                        '-o', str(_BINARY)], check=True, env=env)
    return _BINARY


def run(lines):
    """Run one native invocation and return its stdout lines."""
    result = subprocess.run([str(build())],
                            input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(),
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                            check=False)
    if result.returncode:
        sys.stderr.buffer.write(result.stderr)
        raise RuntimeError('native stage failed')
    return result.stdout.decode().splitlines()


def atlas(routes):
    lines = ['ATLAS ' + str(len(routes))]
    lines += [f'{start:032x} {length} {hop}' for (start, length), hop in routes.items()]
    result = run(lines)
    if len(result) != 1 + int(result[0]):
        raise RuntimeError('native atlas framing')
    rows = [line.split() for line in result[1:]]
    return [int(a, 16) for a, h in rows], [None if h == '-1' else int(h) for a, h in rows]


def pack(starts, hops, tree, addresses):
    nodes = [tree]
    for node in nodes:
        nodes.extend(node['children'])
    indices = {id(n): i for i, n in enumerate(nodes)}
    lines = ['PACK ' + str(len(starts)) + ' ' + str(len(nodes)) + ' ' + str(len(addresses))]
    lines += [f'{x:032x} {-1 if h is None else h}' for x, h in zip(starts, hops)]
    for node in nodes:
        children = [indices[id(c)] for c in node['children']]
        row = [node['lo'], node['span'], node['mode'], node['cached'],
               len(children), *children]
        lines.append(' '.join(map(str, row)))
    lines += [f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]
    output = run(lines)
    if len(output) != len(addresses) + 1:
        raise RuntimeError('native pack framing')
    answers = []
    for line in output[1:]:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, line.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return output[0], answers


def trace(image, addresses):
    rows = run(['TRACE ' + str(len(addresses)), image,
                *[f'{x:032x}' for x in addresses]])
    if len(rows) != len(addresses):
        raise RuntimeError('native trace framing')
    answers = []
    for row in rows:
        hop, rank, count, *path = map(int, row.split())
        if count != len(path):
            raise RuntimeError('native trace path framing')
        answers.append([None if hop == -1 else hop, rank, path])
    return answers


def _decode_nodes(tokens, count):
    """Read `count` breadth-first node records reported by the planner."""
    nodes = []
    offset = 64
    for _ in range(count):
        reported, kind, mode, cached, lo, span, fanout = (int(next(tokens))
                                                          for _ in range(7))
        children = [int(next(tokens)) for _ in range(fanout)]
        keys = (fanout - 1) if kind == 0 else span
        used = 32 + (4 * fanout if kind == 0 else 0) + keys * WIDTH[mode]
        alloc = (used + 63) // 64 * 64
        if reported != offset:
            raise RuntimeError('node offset mismatch')
        nodes.append({"kind": kind, "mode": mode, "cached": cached, "lo": lo,
                      "span": span, "children": children, "offset": offset,
                      "pages": alloc // 64})
        offset += alloc
    return nodes


def solve(cases):
    """Plan and pack every version of every case in one native invocation.

    Each case carries its atlases, its bursts as run indices and its
    costs.  The reply lists, per version, the packed image plus the
    breadth-first node records of the chosen layout.
    """
    lines = ['SOLVE', str(len(cases))]
    for case in cases:
        lines.append('%d %d %d %d %d %d' % (case['cache'], case['hit'], case['miss'],
                                            case['decode'][0], case['decode'][1],
                                            case['decode'][2]))
        lines.append(str(len(case['versions'])))
        for starts, hops in case['versions']:
            lines.append(str(len(starts)))
            lines += ['%032x %d' % (start, -1 if hop is None else hop)
                      for start, hop in zip(starts, hops)]
        lines.append(str(len(case['bursts'])))
        for version, repeat, runs in case['bursts']:
            lines.append('%d %d %d' % (version, repeat, len(runs)))
            lines += [str(run) for run in runs]
    output = run(lines)
    tokens = iter(' '.join(output).split())
    if next(tokens) != 'OK':
        raise RuntimeError('native planner failed')
    layouts = []
    for case in cases:
        planned = []
        for starts, hops in case['versions']:
            image = next(tokens)
            nodes = _decode_nodes(tokens, int(next(tokens)))
            planned.append((image, nodes))
        layouts.append(planned)
    try:
        next(tokens)
    except StopIteration:
        return layouts
    raise RuntimeError('trailing native planner output')

"""Cache-budgeted IPv6 packed-image compiler (protocol 3).

Reads one JSON request through EOF, emits one JSON result.  The Python
driver owns strict validation, the immutable FIB history, the canonical
forwarding atlases and the result shape; the scalar C++ subsystem owns
the joint layout/cache optimisation and the packed image bytes.
"""
import bisect
import json
import sys

import native
import solver
from protocol import Invalid, MAX_INPUT, parse_request

MAX_RUNS_PER_VERSION = 64    # domain bound checked after compilation
MAX_TOTAL_RUNS = 128         # over all committed versions of all cases


def _fib_versions(case):
    """Ordered immutable FIB versions; version 0 is the initial table."""
    routes = {}
    for route, hop in case["initial"]:
        routes[route] = hop                  # aliases collapse, last row wins

    def atlas():
        return solver.compile_atlas((start, length, hop)
                                    for (start, length), hop in routes.items())

    versions = [atlas()]
    for transaction in case["transactions"]:
        for op, route, hop in transaction:
            if op == "set":
                routes[route] = hop          # covered routes survive
            else:
                routes.pop(route, None)      # absent erase is a no-op
        versions.append(atlas())             # even an empty transaction commits
    return versions


def _case_payload(case):
    """Normalised planning input: atlases plus per-version burst traffic."""
    versions = _fib_versions(case)
    per_version = [[] for _ in versions]
    bursts = []
    for version, repeat, addresses in case["bursts"]:
        starts = versions[version][0]
        runs = [bisect.bisect_right(starts, address) - 1 for address in addresses]
        bursts.append((version, repeat, runs))
        per_version[version].append((repeat, runs))
    return {"cache": case["cache_pages"], "hit": case["costs"][0],
            "miss": case["costs"][1], "decode": list(case["costs"][2]),
            "versions": versions, "bursts": bursts, "per_version": per_version}


def compile_request(cases):
    """Compile every case, or reject the whole request, before any output."""
    result = {"cases": []}
    if not cases:
        return result
    payloads = []
    total_runs = 0
    for case in cases:
        payload = _case_payload(case)
        for starts, _hops in payload["versions"]:
            if len(starts) > MAX_RUNS_PER_VERSION:
                raise Invalid("version run bound")
            total_runs += len(starts)
        if total_runs > MAX_TOTAL_RUNS:
            raise Invalid("request run bound")
        payloads.append(payload)
    layouts = native.solve(payloads)
    for case, payload, planned in zip(cases, payloads, layouts):
        versions = payload["versions"]
        out_versions = []
        layout_objects = []
        for (starts, hops), (image, nodes) in zip(versions, planned):
            out_versions.append({"starts": [format(start, "032x") for start in starts],
                                 "hops": list(hops), "image": image})
            layout_objects.append(solver.Layout(starts, hops, image, nodes))
        changes = [solver.compute_changes(versions[index][0], versions[index][1],
                                          versions[index + 1][0],
                                          versions[index + 1][1])
                   for index in range(len(versions) - 1)]
        bursts = [solver.layout_answers(layout_objects[version], runs)
                  for version, _repeat, runs in payload["bursts"]]
        objective = solver.case_objective(layout_objects, payload["per_version"],
                                         case["costs"])
        result["cases"].append({"versions": out_versions, "changes": changes,
                                "bursts": bursts, "objective": objective})
    return result


def main():
    try:
        cases = parse_request(sys.stdin.buffer.read(MAX_INPUT + 1))
        result = compile_request(cases)
    except Invalid:
        result = {"error": "invalid"}
    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Architecture

**Python driver** (`main.py`, `protocol.py`, `solver.py`, `native.py`):
- Strict request validation (duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, extra JSON values, type/range/domain bounds) rejecting the whole request with exactly `{"error":"invalid"}`.
- Immutable FIB history: route aliasing/normalization, last-row-wins, ordered transactions (each commits a version, even empty ones), covering routes preserved so withdrawals reveal the right fallback.
- Canonical atlas compilation with exact 128-bit arithmetic (boundary sweep + longest-prefix max-heap).
- Domain checks that require compilation: `R ≤ 64` per version, `≤ 128` summed over all versions of all cases.
- Forwarding changes (sorted, disjoint, coalesced, `U` bounds), burst answer paths and the exact objective.

**C++17 scalar library** (`engine.hpp`, `engine.cpp`):
- `ATLAS` — full-width maximal forwarding runs (`unsigned __int128`).
- `PACK`/`TRACE` — exact FIDX image construction and byte-level packed lookup.
- `SOLVE` — the joint optimiser.

## The optimiser
An exact interval DP over `[i,j)` run ranges: node options (leaf span 1..8 / internal fanout 2..9, encoding modes 0–2 with the 2⁶⁴/2³² spread legality tests, cached/uncached) are combined with children forests, carrying a resident-page dimension as a monotone array merged by min-plus convolution. The lexicographic `(work, image_pages)` pair is carried in one integer as `work·PAGE_WEIGHT + pages`, so both objectives are minimized jointly and exactly. Versions are coupled only through the shared page budget, folded with the same convolution, then the allocation is back-tracked and each tree is reconstructed by exact value matching, re-ordered breadth-first and packed.

The burst-aware cost model computes the fetch weight `T` from each burst's own next-run cursor — necessary because a burst whose runs straddle a node range without entering it must fetch nothing.
